# Architecture

Instrumentation stack for a 63V/100A coaxial BLDC inverter. TIM1 and the synced current path are configured and reachable; **no control law is** - commutation and the current loop belong above `Board/` and beside `Comms/`, and nothing there exists yet. Layering is strict: components only know the abstraction immediately below them, allowing protocol or transport swaps without cascading edits.

## Firmware

* **`Core/`**: Autogenerated CubeMX initialization. User code is the two sensor poll calls and `Board_StoKeepalive()`, which must stay at the top of the loop - `link_active()` does a `continue`.
* **`Board/`**: Concrete hardware implementation (`adc`, `cal`, `clock`, `io`, `imu`, `angle`, `pwm`, `sync`, `sto`, `log`, `daq`, `selftest`) of `board.h`. `board_pwm.c` and `board_sync.c` use CMSIS rather than the `htim1` handle: clearing MOE has to be one store that cannot fail partway. Unidirectional dependency. `board_imu.c` and `board_angle.c` each carry a poll loop the main loop advances, writing a shared record the command layer reads - the host never drives a bus. `board_log.c` is one ring every source pushes into, so a host can take fifteen samples per round trip instead of one; producers span an ISR and the main loop, which is why the critical section is PRIMASK and not a mutex this board has no scheduler for. `board_daq.c` is one configured acquisition task - channels, clock, sampling window, decimation, accumulation - buffering raw bytes whose stride the config decides, and describing its own record layout so no host holds a copy of the shape.
* **`Modbus/`**: Hardware-agnostic RTU stack (CRC, PDU, framing). Pure C standard library, zero CMSIS/HAL. Driven by lookup tables, not switches.
* **`Comms/`**: Command dispatch and the wire. `wire.h` enforces total accessors with sticky error flags, eliminating per-field `if` branching. `cmd_device.c` is the one function code left (`0x6E`) fronting every peripheral by device byte; `cmd_imu.c`, `cmd_angle.c`, `cmd_link.c`, `cmd_cal.c`, `cmd_bridge.c`, `cmd_log.c` and `cmd_daq.c` are its op dispatchers. `dev_uart.c` is the only file that touches a USART or its interrupt, and `link.c` runs one RTU state machine per port over three of them - one slave, three wires, and the unit id belongs to the board.
* **`Shtp/`**: The BNO08X's transport framing. Portable C11 like `Modbus/`, and host-tested the same way by `test_shtp_core.py`.

## Host

* **`host/coaxial/`**: Python library grouped by hardware function. Topology, pin maps and the parts list are dynamically queried from the board to eliminate hardcoded assumptions. `orientation.py`, `dial.py` and `desk.py` are pure character renderers - a reading in, text out - so all three are tested without a board; `mesh.py` reduces the CAD export in `render/models` to a surface the first can draw.
* **`host/coaxial_mcp/`**: MCP server optimized for LLM token constraints. Emits dense fixed-column text (8.8x smaller than JSON). Probes OS ports and ST-Links for Modbus responses, gracefully falling back to a duck-typed `SimulatedSession`. Supports multi-node segments (Unit 0 = broadcast).
* **`host/coaxial_ollama/`**: Local LLM orchestrator. Manages execution loops, context scaling, tool routing, and stateless mid-session hardware/model hot-swaps.

## Scaling & Validation

* **Scaling**: Firmware exposes raw ADC ticks. The host dictates physical conversions (NTC parameters, divider ratios) to isolate hardware revisions. Legacy board-side scaling is retained strictly to cross-verify the math.
* **Structure suite**: ~3 s, no board and no model. Every module under `host/` except the suites themselves - `testline/` and `examples/` were outside it for no reason and had never been checked. Every module imports cold, no import cycles, no definition copied into two files, no dead imports, nothing past 130 lines or 7 deep (async functions included: `AsyncFunctionDef` is not a subclass of `FunctionDef`, so three handlers were exempt without anyone deciding it), every module and class documented. It exists because the behavioural suites import what they need and pass while the rest of the package is broken - measured, five NameErrors in one afternoon of moving code.
* **Testing**: Seventeen suites, 1663 checks (structure, Modbus core, SHTP core, seven ollama suites, MCP, simulated, parity, conformance, live model). The core suite builds `modbus_crc/slave/rtu` with the host gcc and drives them through ctypes with the tick counter injected, so t1.5, t3.5 and the 2^32 wrap are tested by arithmetic rather than by waiting - the only check on that code that needs no cable. A missing compiler skips it, the way a missing cable skips conformance; `setup.ps1` installs one. `run_tests.ps1` is the only interface: `-AutomaticMinimal|Medium|High` run ~25/50/75 % of every check, `-All` the gate, `-Only NAMES` and `-Tags SUBJECTS` one change's worth, `-Structure` the package itself. A disconnected board triggers the simulated fallback, not a failure; conformance needs hardware. So does parity, which skips itself rather than compare a stand-in with a stand-in - so the stand-in's channel table is also checked against `s_adcTable` read straight out of `board_adc.c`, in `test_simulated.py`, on the run that costs three seconds and no cable.
* **Test selection**: The local LLM reads the diff and names the suites, the subjects inside the big one, and the live section (`tools|sequence|language|none`). The path map is the fallback, used only when no model answers - it is coarse by construction, pulling four suites for any line in one file. Every unusable reply means run everything. A narrowed run still draws one test from each subject left out, and coverage is measured in checks, not groups (2 to 77 per group).
* **A fixture must build what the product builds.** The live suite configured its own client and passed for weeks on a configuration nobody ran: with `think` unset the model called `analog_read`, with `think=False` - what the prompt sends - the same question called `board_info`.
